subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should backup excludes be accepted only as explicit user-requested filters on current main, or may OpenClaw also auto-load a state-dir `.backupignore` and ship the current protected-path/external-asset semantics?
rationale: Backup selection controls what data is restorable and what sensitive files leave the machine, so the permanent product/security boundary needs maintainer intent before repair automation can safely choose semantics.

options.title: Require explicit, current-main-safe excludes
options.body: Rework this PR so `.backupignore` is opt-in, filters apply per asset root, current backup safety behavior is preserved, and proof shows real backup/verify behavior.

options.title: Accept implicit state-dir policy
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly approve auto-loading `.backupignore` and the current warning-only external-asset behavior, but they would own the compatibility and security tradeoff.

options.title: Pause or replace the branch
options.body: If the stale branch is too costly to preserve, close or replace it with a narrower current-main PR that credits this implementation and the earlier community PRs.

recommendation.title: Require explicit, current-main-safe excludes
recommendation.body: Rework this PR so `.backupignore` is opt-in, filters apply per asset root, current backup safety behavior is preserved, and proof shows real backup/verify behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: gumadeiras merged the original local backup CLI and authored adjacent backup path/verify hardening, making them the best available owner for backup restore/security semantics.
